summary: Ch.1: Yu Xiyu, youngest member of the hit boy band GREATEST, looks out at a sold-out 10,000-seat stadium and remembers growing up poor with his single mother. Scouted in eighth grade, he was picked over a better-connected trainee because the executive liked his innocent smile, after his mother handed over all her savings. Coached to play the sweet, spoiled youngest, he privately looks after his teammates. Driving home after a concert he stops alone at a dark park toilet, hears clicking, and finds a stalker fan pressed against the window holding an XI <3 YU sign.

Ch.2: The stalker fans at the park toilet window beg for a hug; Xiyu shoves them off and yells. Running back, one slips into the filth. Next morning reporters crowd the dorm: an edited surveillance video on Weibo claims Xiyu lured and humiliated female fans. Ruiyang promises to stand by him. The president refuses to pay for damage control or hear him out, holds him responsible and tells him to pay the contract penalty -- he is out of the group.

Ch.3: Fans stage a sit-down protest that blocks the dorm exit; online abuse targets Xiyu and his mother. Trainees mock him; Song Wei punches one for a vile insult. Zhang Suihan bluntly tells him he lacks talent but should plan his future and that the band will help. Trying to leave, Xiyu is mobbed and pelted with noodles and sent back. He decides not to waste his mother's savings: he asks Ruiyang to lend him a year's tuition for a better school, and Ruiyang, who is rich, agrees.
